Active-sensing blood pressure wristband · complete design

The same sensors and world model, moved to the wrist

Simulation + CADSame sensors and the same on-device world model as the ring, moved to the radial artery at the wrist. The band has about 16 times the battery energy and room for a display. Everything below is a simulated design and a CAD model: nothing has been built or measured. The ring version has its own page.

Renders

Where it sits on the wrist

The sensor pod is offset 13 mm towards the thumb and tilted 19 degrees so its window lies flat over the radial artery, against the radius bone. Electronics only cross the thumb side of the strap; the clasp is on the other side.

What still has to be custom

  • Sensor tile, 4 x 9 mm: laser, speckle imager and PMUT in one package (imec).
  • Ultrasound tile front end (one per tile) and receiver ASIC (imec), same dies as the ring.
  • Everything else is catalogue parts in normal packages. In the ring, almost every block needs bare die or WLCSP.

Electronics, revision B (after the expert panel)

Two boards joined by an 8-line flex moulded into the strap. The sensor pod has its own controller, safety supervisor, rails, 24 V supply and the ring's Class 1 laser circuit, so no interlock or analog line crosses the strap: only battery power (current-limited, fused), ground, a UART link, sync and wake. Netlist and BOM in bp-band/hardware/electronics/out/.

Simulation at the wrist, v2

The ring simulator with wrist physiology, after the panel fixes: the ultrasound feature that leaked blood pressure is removed, power comes from a per-component model, and the model was retrained and retuned. 96 held-out virtual wearers, 24 hours each. Primary result: ISO 81060-2 style, against a simulated auscultatory reference (two observers, sequential readings on the same arm, observer and cuff error modelled), so the device is not scored against a truth no real test has. Arterial-truth numbers are secondary. 95% confidence intervals come from resampling wearers. No per-wearer calibration in the main numbers. Battery days run from an aged cell (80% capacity) to a new one, both at 90% usable. The earlier band numbers (± 5.8 mmHg, 23 days) came from the leaky simulator and are withdrawn.

What the wrist simulation says, v2

  • Accuracy at the ISO edge. Balanced mode: SBP −0.1 ± 7.7 mmHg against a simulated auscultatory reference (SD 95% CI 6.6 to 8.8), both ISO 81060-2 criteria pass, at 3.04 mW including the display: 11.4 to 14.3 days. The upper confidence limit is above the ISO limit of 8.
  • It rests on an assumed speckle signal. At half the assumed strength the band fails ISO: +0.6 ± 10.8. That number has to come from a bench measurement on wrists.
  • Saver and max-accuracy modes do not earn their names. Saver (2.07 mW, 16.8 to 21 days) fails ISO at ± 9.1. Max accuracy uses 5 mW (6.9 to 8.6 days) and is no more accurate than balanced (+0.5 ± 7.6, fails criterion 2). Only balanced is a validated configuration today.
  • Speckle carries the result; ultrasound adds nothing measurable in simulation. Without speckle: −10.1 ± 14.8. Without ultrasound: +0.2 ± 7.7 at the same power. Ultrasound fires on 0.1% of steps. PPG alone: −12.6 ± 15.0.
  • Active control beats an equal-energy timer by a little: SD 0.61 mmHg better (CI 0.31 to 0.86); the timer fails ISO (−0.3 ± 8.7).
  • It does not react to blood pressure yet. Costly readings are only 1.04 times as frequent when pressure moves as when it is stable. 20 mmHg rises are caught 41% of the time (timer 44%) with 7.4 false alarms per day. Honest description: scheduled baseline plus event-triggered checks.
  • The range is right on average, not per reading. After conformal calibration 95% of errors fall inside the 95% range, but its width does not track the actual error (correlation 0.02) and the worst 5% of wearers get 78% coverage.
  • A month later, put back on with drifted sensor offsets: +0.4 ± 7.4 with no cuff; 3 cuff readings requested by the model with a per-wearer update: −0.5 ± 6.9. Cuff readings help a little; the device reduces cuff calibration, it does not remove it.

Read every number as a design gate, not a result. The links from blood pressure to the sensor features are assumptions in a simulator, the reference is simulated, and nothing has been measured on a wrist. The full list of what the expert panel found and what changed is in bp-audit/v2/FIX_LOG.md.

Against the design brief

Layer mapping and gaps: bp-band/hardware/architecture_vs_brief.md. Token format v0.1: bp-band/firmware/bpb_token.h.

Brief requirementBand now
No reading without a questionNot met: most costly readings come from a baseline schedule
Surprise is the signalNot shown: trigger does not follow real BP change (ratio 1.04)
Competing hypotheses, sequential tests, stopping ruleGap: threshold ladder today
Output is a belief with honest confidencePartial: calibrated on average, width not informative
Learning each wearerSimulated only: requested cuff readings with a Bayesian offset update; not in firmware
Independent safety supervisorIn the revision B schematic: pod supervisor U211 owns laser, HV and ultrasound enables
Energy metering per rail, common clockIn the schematic: rail shunts read while on; one clock with a sync line

Reviews and what changed

Two reviews so far. An audit against the design brief (audit report, bp-audit/audit/compliance_matrix.md) found that the ultrasound flow feature in the simulator was a near-direct blood pressure readout, that most costly readings came from a timer, and that the confidence range was right only on average. An expert panel then listed 54 defects across both designs (20 blockers). The leak is removed from this page's simulator, the strap wiring is redesigned with a pod controller and supervisor, the power model is per component, and every number on this page is from the v2 evaluation. Each defect, what changed, what was checked and what is still open: bp-audit/v2/FIX_LOG.md.

Still open, the short list: no hardware measurements; the speckle signal strength is assumed; the controller does not yet key on real pressure change; the range width does not track the error; the per-wearer update is not in firmware; ultrasound coupling at 10 MHz depends on imec PMUT numbers.

Wording: "reduces, not eliminates, cuff calibration" and "no one we found combines direct artery sensing with active reasoning".
